Nov 2023

Jacob Vogel receives H.M. Queen Silvia's Prize

Jacob Vogel received H.M. Queen Silvia's Prize for a young Alzheimer's researcher, instituted by Alzheimerfonden, at a ceremony at the German Church in Stockholm. The prize recognizes his contributions to Alzheimer's research, including work suggesting four distinct types of the disease and evidence that tau can spread through the brain along neurons.

Nov 2026

New preprint: how aging beyond the brain relates to neurodegenerative disease

A new preprint led by Romina Zendehdel, which began as her master's thesis, uses plasma proteomics from over 50,000 UK Biobank participants to show how the biological aging of different organs relates to brain structure and neurodegenerative disease risk. Congratulations, Romina and team!

Oct 2026

New preprint: a coordinated multicellular response to Alzheimer's disease

In her first PhD project, Gabriele Vilkaite built a single model integrating AD-related changes across neurons and glia, revealing a coordinated multicellular signature associated with pathology. The signature replicated in a completely independent dataset and was linked to faster cognitive decline. Congratulations, Gabi and team!

Oct 2026

New paper in Nature Neuroscience: aging and Alzheimer's reshape the brain along different axes

Led by PhD student Jonathan Rittmo, this work looks at how functional connectivity reorganizes in aging and Alzheimer's disease along distinct axes of functional brain organization. Congratulations, Jonathan and team!

Sep 2026

New preprint: data leakage inflates protein biomarker studies

A new preprint led by Lijun An quantifies one common reason why proteomics biomarker studies are hard to replicate: data leakage. Even pure noise can look like a biomarker. The preprint also introduces two open tools to catch leakage, Leakly for pipelines and Plumber for manuscripts.

Read the preprint

Apr 2026

New paper in Nature Medicine: diagnosing neurodegenerative diseases from blood

Lijun An and colleagues present ProtAIDe-Dx, an AI-proteomics model that diagnoses multiple neurodegenerative diseases from blood plasma. The model was validated for real-world clinical questions, including differential diagnosis in a memory clinic setting.

Read the paper

Join us to model how tau spreads through the brain in Alzheimer's disease, using large tau-PET datasets.
